name: The pointwise energy conditions NEC, WEC, SEC, DEC over timelike/null observers, and 'the DEC requires the WEC'

source.located: Hawking & Ellis 1973, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time, sec. 4.3 (pp. 88-96): the pointwise conditions and the Hawking-Ellis type classification. READ through two arXiv restatements that quote the definitions exactly: Curiel 2014, 'A Primer on Energy Conditions', arXiv:1405.0403 p. 5-8 (geometric/physical/effective forms of NEC, WEC, SEC, DEC, SDEC; follows Hawking-Ellis 1973 p. 89, Visser 1996 ch. 12, Malament 2012); Kontou & Sanders 2020, 'Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory', arXiv:2003.01815 sec. 2.1, eqs (18)-(27), Table 1, Figure 2, Props 2.1-2.2 (Tipler 1978). Cross-read: Fliss 2026 Modave lectures arXiv:2605.18964 Lecture 1 (eqs 1.5-1.18).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1405.0403 (pages 1-2, 5-9, 12-13, 30, 32), 2003.01815 (pages 1-3, 5-6, 8-11, 14-15, 49), 2605.18964 (pages 1-10, 16-17, 20, 24, 45, 48). Hawking-Ellis 1973 itself is pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ; Curiel p. 5 cites it by page (p. 89) for the type-I classification and both restatements give the four definitions in identical form.

published_statement: Curiel 2014 p. 6 (physical forms): NEC -- for any null vector k^a, T_mn k^m k^n >= 0; WEC -- for any timelike vector xi^a, T_mn xi^m xi^n >= 0; SEC -- for any timelike xi^a, (T_mn - (1/2) T g_mn) xi^m xi^n >= 0; DEC -- (1) for any timelike xi^a, T_mn xi^m xi^n >= 0, AND T^a_n xi^n is causal; equivalently (2) for any two co-oriented timelike xi^a, eta^a, T_mn xi^m eta^n >= 0. Effective (type-I) forms, same page: NEC rho + p_i >= 0 each i; WEC rho >= 0 and rho + p_i >= 0; SEC rho + sum p_i >= 0 and rho + p_i >= 0; DEC rho >= 0 and |p_i| <= rho. Curiel p. 8: 'the SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC'; p. 7: 'the WEC implies the NEC'; p. 8: 'The SEC does not imply the WEC ... The SEC does, however, imply the NEC.' Kontou-Sanders 2020 eq. (23) and p. 10: the DEC 'is equivalent to the WEC (18), with the additional requirement that -T^a_b t^b is a future-pointing causal vector field'; eq. (20): SEC in n dimensions is (T_ab - T g_ab/(n-2)) t^a t^b >= 0; eq. (24): DEC <=> in any orthonormal frame T_00 >= |T_mu nu|; Table 1 and Figure 2 give the implications DEC => WEC => NEC and SEC => NEC.
published_hypotheses: Pointwise: each condition is imposed at a spacetime point on the stress tensor T_ab picked out by the Einstein field equation (Curiel fn. 1); the geometric forms (R_ab k^a k^b >= 0 etc.) are equivalent to the physical forms only when the field equation holds (Curiel p. 5).
The vectors quantified over are ALL null (NEC) or ALL timelike (WEC, SEC, DEC) vectors at the point, co-oriented (future-pointing) for the DEC's two-vector form (Curiel p. 6; K-S eq. 23).

The effective (rho, p_i) forms presuppose a Hawking-Ellis type-I (diagonalisable) stress tensor, 'no serious restriction' for known classical fields except a null fluid (Curiel p. 5 and fn. 10); for DEC vs SDEC the effective forms coincide only for type I (Curiel p. 6).
SEC's 1/2 is the four-dimensional value of 1/(n-2) (K-S eq. 20; Fliss eq. 1.13).

The conditions are normalisation-free for the NEC (scale invariance, K-S Prop. 2.1); for WEC/SEC/DEC on unit timelike vectors a finite lower bound need not be zero, but any finite lower bound already implies the NEC (Tipler 1978; K-S Prop. 2.2, proved without the type-I assumption).

Physical standing, not part of the definition: the sources state the conditions are violated by non-minimally coupled scalars classically (K-S sec. 2.3, Table 2) and by every quantum field theory pointwise (K-S p. 3, Fliss Lecture 3), and that the SEC is violated by a positive cosmological constant / dark energy and by inflation (Curiel p. 30, 32).
hypothesis_drift: NONE for certify.py's definitions: NEC/WEC/SEC forms at certify.py:336-350 match Curiel p. 6 exactly (SEC as T(V,V) + T/2 with trace = eta^mn T_mn, verified equal to (T_ab - T g_ab/2)V^aV^b for unit V); 'DEC requires the WEC' (certify.py:85, 353-355) is the source's DEC clause (1) read in the direction not-WEC => not-DEC; V = gamma(1, s u) is unit timelike (checked).

ADDED (owner-named, not a drift against the source): certify.py:326-350 samples 200 null directions and 10 speeds s <= 10/11, so a reported violation is a witness and a reported satisfaction a floor; further, when the NEC fails the true WEC/SEC infimum over unit timelike observers is -infinity (K-S Prop. 2.2 contrapositive; shown in rederive section D), so the 'WEC min'/'SEC min' columns at certify.py:76-82 are grid-dependent sample values, not invariants. The NEC column is invariant up to sampling (exact min(rho+p_r, rho+p_T) at r = 1 is -8.8138e-4 against the sampled -8.7348e-4).

certify.py:96, :456 (prose and selftest pin) state T_00(r=1) = -4.8455e-4 and 'a ratio of 1.21'; the file's own table at :80 and the exact closed form T_{tt} = e^{2Phi}(2 Lap Phi - |grad Phi|^2) both give -4.6564e-4 (ratio 1.165). near() at :409-411 is tol*max(1,|want|) = 1e-3 ABSOLUTE there, so the pin passes without discriminating. A discrepancy, recorded, not a refutation: sign and conclusion unchanged.

bounds.py:43, 94-95, 295 'zero (the NEC's RHS) ... saturated by the vacuum and by EM': the vacuum saturates for every null k (T = 0); the electromagnetic field does NOT -- T_ab k^a k^b = |F_ab k^b|^2 >= 0 with equality only when k is a principal null direction of F (Coulomb: E^2(1 - n_x^2), zero only along +-E; plane wave: A^2(1 - n_x)^2, zero only along the wave). The only EM field with T_kk = 0 for every null k is F = 0. Neither source says EM saturates the NEC; K-S eq. (36)-(38) say the Maxwell field SATISFIES NEC/WEC/DEC/SEC (sum of squares) and is traceless in n = 4. The row's coding S = 0 'known saturated' is over-broad as worded; the trace-free condition, not the NEC, is what EM saturates.

phase1.py:195-197, 537-539 'No energy condition ... is violated by D1-D5 with M_ADM = 0' is asserted, not computed, and is contradicted by the tree's own results under the definition as read: certify.py:84-85 computes every condition violated at every sampled radius of the seated ansatz, and certify.py:110-125's ansatz-free theorem (dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho, contraction iff m(r) < 0) with phase1.py:203-204, 558-559 'every line needs M < 0' forces rho < 0 somewhere, i.e. T(u,u) < 0 for the static observer -- a pointwise WEC failure and hence (DEC => WEC) a DEC failure. M_ADM = 0 does not rescue a pointwise condition. This is the one in-tree statement that drops a hypothesis of the source (pointwise, all observers) by reading the condition as a statement about total mass.

nonstatic.py:324-325, 351-355: k_rad's nullness is a checked identity, k_trn = (e^-Phi, 0, 1/R, 0)'s is not; verified null here (section E), and T(k_trn,k_trn) = rho + p_T, T(k_rad,k_rad) = rho + p_r - 2j with j = T^{t r} (outward flux) reproduced. No drift; one unchecked identity now checked.

formation.py:169-197 uses the NEC pointwise along a family and then integrates T_kk over Eulerian proper time; the integrated quantity is an in-tree construct (owner's THEOREM F2), not an averaged energy condition of the source -- neither ANEC (affine parameter along a complete null geodesic) nor a QEI. Not a drift in the definition; the owner's word THEOREM covers only its own residual-checked identity.

latticectc.py:84-90, 150 evaluates the NEC on a stress tensor read off a hand-written 5-D metric's Einstein tensor. The definition is dimension-free for the NEC (K-S Table 1), so no drift; note only that a 5-D SEC would need T/3 not T/2 (K-S eq. 20) -- the tree does not use SEC there.

seatindex.py:93-94, 376-377 and dichotomy.py:155-156 identify T_kk > 0 with 'energy-condition-satisfying matter': correct as a necessary condition (NEC along that k) and as the sign the seating threshold needs; it is not a claim that the WEC/DEC hold, and the owners do not make one.

rederivation.outcome: 40 checks, 0 failed (sympy 1.14, z3 5.1, numeric via import of certify.py). A: z3 proves on type-I effective forms DEC => WEC, WEC => NEC, SEC => NEC, DEC => NEC and not-WEC => not-DEC; witnesses for WEC =/=> SEC (rho=1/2, p=-1/2,-1/2,0), SEC =/=> WEC (rho=-1/4, p=1/4), NEC =/=> WEC, WEC =/=> DEC. B: z3 (nonlinear real, quantified) proves WEC_phys <=> (rho>=0, rho+p_i>=0) and NEC_phys <=> (rho+p_i>=0) for a diagonal tensor. C: sympy: (T_ab - T g_ab/2)V^aV^b == T(V,V) + T/2 for unit V, certify's V is unit timelike, 1/(n-2) = 1/2 at n=4. D: T(V,V) = (rho + s^2 sum p_i u_i^2)/(1-s^2) and the WEC infimum is -oo when the NEC fails. E: k_rad and k_trn null; T(k_rad,k_rad) = rho + p_r - 2j; T(k_trn,k_trn) = rho + p_T; k = u + n with -u.k = 1. F: EM T_kk = |F_ab k^b|^2; Coulomb and plane-wave witnesses show EM does not saturate the NEC for all k. G: certify's table rows r = 0.2, 1, 10 reproduced to 0.2 %; closed form T_tt = e^{2Phi}(2 Lap Phi - |grad Phi|^2) derived from the conformastatic metric and evaluated exactly at r = 1: -4.65637e-4 (matches the table, not the selftest pin -4.8455e-4 -- recorded); rho < 0 at r = 1 so WEC fails for the static observer alone. H: m(r1) < 0 with dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho forces rho < 0 somewhere, which with DEC => WEC contradicts phase1.py:195-197 as worded.

later_literature.what: Restates the four conditions in n dimensions (SEC with T/(n-2)), proves Tipler's two propositions without the type-I assumption (Props 2.1-2.2), gives Table 2 of classical fields: Maxwell/Proca satisfy all four, non-minimally coupled scalars violate all four on-shell, minimally coupled scalar with V >= 0 violates only the SEC; all pointwise conditions violated by every QFT; AANEC as the candidate universal condition.

later_literature.ref: Curiel 2014, arXiv:1405.0403 (Towards a Theory of Spacetime Theories, 2017)
later_literature.what: The definitions as the tree uses them, plus the catalogue of violations (Curiel p. 30-32): WEC violated necessarily by traversable wormholes and 'hyper-fast' travel (Alcubierre 1994, Krasnikov 1998, Olum 1998); SEC violated necessarily by inflation and by dark energy; NEC violated classically by scalar-field models. Narrows the conditions' standing as universal matter constraints, not their definitions.

Lecture 1 eqs (1.5)-(1.18) restate WEC, DEC (as two-vector form, equivalent to WEC plus t^mu t^nu T^alpha_mu T_alpha nu <= 0), SEC with 1/(d-2), NEC; shows Yang-Mills (hence Maxwell) satisfies all four with T_kk = tr(F_AB F^AB)/2g^2 >= 0 (eq. 1.37) -- satisfied, not saturated; Lecture 3: every QFT violates every pointwise condition and smeared expectation values are unbounded below (Witten's scaling argument); ANEC proven for all Minkowski QFTs, AANEC needed on compact directions.

later_literature.ref: Hollands, Longo & Morsella 2026, 'A Quantum Dominant Energy Condition', arXiv:2608.01814
later_literature.what: States the classical DEC as T_mn k^m u^n >= 0 for future-pointing causal u, k, 'implies the NEC as a special case'; notes the DEC fails arbitrarily badly at a point for suitable QFT states; proposes a QDEC (information-energy tradeoff) proven for Rindler wedges, reducing for coherent states of a free scalar to the classical DEC of the underlying solution. Quantum replacement of the DEC, as QNEC is of the NEC.

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Kontou 2020, arXiv:1907.13604; Fewster & Galloway 2011, arXiv:1012.6038; Bousso et al. 2015, arXiv:1506.02669 (QFC); Hollands-Longo-Morsella 2025 arXiv:2503.04651 (QNEC proof); Engelhardt-Nagar 2026 arXiv:2605.05326
later_literature.what: Singularity theorems re-proved from weakened (averaged, smeared, semiclassical) energy hypotheses and quantum focusing; a 2026 semiclassical singularity theorem without the null energy condition. The pointwise conditions remain the classical special case.

lacked_data: What Hawking and Ellis (1973) lacked: the accelerated expansion (1998; Planck 2018 Omega_Lambda = 0.6847 +/- 0.0073, w_0 = -1.028 +/- 0.031), which shows the SEC violated on cosmological scales today (Curiel p. 32 says Visser predicted this on SEC grounds in 1997 before the data); the systematic classical NEC violations of non-minimally coupled scalars (Barcelo-Visser and later, K-S sec. 2.3); the general ANEC proofs in Minkowski QFT (2016) and the QNEC/QDEC programme (2015-2026). Pointwise quantum violations were already known in 1965 (Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe), so the 1973 authors did not lack that. Does having the data change the conclusion? For the DEFINITIONS -- no: they are definitions, and every implication among them re-derives unchanged (z3, section A-B). For their PHYSICAL AUTHORITY -- yes, and in a specific direction: the literature since 1973 has demoted the pointwise conditions from universal matter constraints to a classical special case, with averaged/quantum conditions (ANEC/AANEC, QEIs, QNEC, QDEC) as the ones expected to bind. Evidence for M's hypothesis: the tree's 'refused currency' (latticectc.py:84-87) treats a pointwise NEC failure as decisive, while Fliss 2026 and K-S 2020 say every QFT violates every pointwise condition, so a pointwise failure alone is not the physically binding fact. Evidence against M's hypothesis: certify.py's refusal rests on a COMPUTED violation of magnitude six orders above the noise floor across all radii of a fixed classical metric, and no later datum reverses a computation on a fixed metric; the tree also already seats the averaged/quantum family beside the pointwise one (bounds.py, necindex), so it has not been misled by the demotion. The unresolved question the data raise -- whether the seated ansatz's violation survives the QEI/ANEC bounds -- belongs to the Ford-Roman / ANEC rows, not to this one.
grade_evidence: The statement and hypotheses as used in certify.py:336-355 are the source's exactly (Curiel p. 6; K-S Table 1): NEC over null k, WEC over timelike V, SEC as T(V,V) + T/2 (verified equal to the (T_ab - T g_ab/2) form for unit V in n = 4), and 'DEC requires the WEC' is DEC clause (1) by definition in both restatements (K-S p. 10: 'equivalent to the WEC with the additional requirement'); z3 proves DEC => WEC and the non-implications the sources state. nonstatic.py's contractions T_kk = rho + p_r -/+ 2j and rho + p_T re-derive exactly, and k_trn's nullness (unchecked by the owner) is verified here. certify's table rows are reproduced to 0.2 % by import and the T_00 closed form derived independently agrees with the table. No numerical datum enters the definitions; Omega_Lambda moves only the SEC's standing as a matter assumption, which no owner relies on. Three in-tree discrepancies are recorded against owners, none against the external result: certify.py:96/:456's pin -4.8455e-4 vs its own table -4.6564e-4 (misprint-class, non-discriminating tolerance); bounds.py:43/295's 'saturated by EM' (EM satisfies, and saturates only along principal null directions -- computed); phase1.py:195-197's 'no energy condition is violated' (contradicted by the tree's own M < 0 requirement under the definition as read -- computed in section H). The last is the drift a reader of phase1 must know: it does not narrow the external result, it misstates it in one owner.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if an owner is found relying on the SEC (or the DEC) as a physical constraint on admissible matter rather than as a computed classification -- none does now. WRONG only if a counterexample to DEC => WEC, WEC => NEC or SEC => NEC were exhibited, which z3 rules out on type I and the sources' vector-form proofs (Curiel p. 7-8, K-S Fig. 2) rule out generally; or if certify's energy_conditions() were shown to mis-evaluate a condition (it does not: the exact NEC minimum brackets the sampled one). The grade does not depend on the in-tree discrepancies; repairing or not repairing them leaves STANDS. Hawking-Ellis 1973 sec. 4.3 read at source would move read_status from READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT to READ but cannot move the grade, since both restatements agree verbatim on the four definitions.
